title: Case: Repaired machine part at the destination depot with an incomplete address on the label
context: A joinery business sent a spindle drive abroad to its maker for warranty repair. The repaired part came back through the border and reached the Ashgrove Arc destination depot nearest the business.
initial_request: Tracking still says return in progress. It goes at half five tomorrow morning, does it not? Has it been stopped or has it not? I have told you the unit, I have told you the account. What else does anybody need? Is anyone doing anything?

acceptable_actions.summary: Request a return hold on DL-8918 before the 8 Apr 05:30 trunk, giving the consignee's unit number and account for verification.
Same return-hold request to the Recovery team through Dispatch chat.

must: Requests a return hold on DL-8918 from the Recovery team, Ashgrove Arc Logistics, by Email or Dispatch chat, and states the cut-off: the border trunk leaves 8 Apr 05:30.
Gives the address detail for the owning team to verify (Unit 7, Millrace Yard, as stated by the consignee; business account PA-B-4471) and asks them to confirm whether the hold is placed.
Says that the earlier correction on the Depot work queue was closed automatically and changed nothing.

Tells the Recovery team why the hold is urgent: the consignee has come forward for a repaired part, and according to the repairer a return means a fresh export declaration and at least three more weeks.
must_not: Tells the business that the return has been stopped, the address corrected or the parcel released, when the queue item was closed with no change made.
Tells the business to have the repairer resend the part with a corrected address.
Resubmits the correction on the Depot work queue, which does not accept it for shipments in return.
States who will pay for a second carriage or customs paperwork, or that no new paperwork will be needed.
Sends the business a holding reply that only says the matter is being looked into, without acting on the route the queue named before the trunk leaves.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Return hold request, time-critical: DL-8918, import from Varga Drivetech to Kestrel Vale Joinery. It is in export-return staging at the destination depot and leaves on the border trunk on 8 Apr at 05:30. It was flagged undeliverable on 6 Apr because the label has no unit number and no consignee phone. The consignee, workshop manager Isolde Kittering, states the address is Unit 7, Millrace Yard, and that this matches their Ashgrove Arc business account PA-B-4471, which he says receives deliveries at that address most weeks. Please verify against the account and tell me whether you can hold the return and release it for delivery. I sent this correction to the Depot work queue at 09:05 today; it was closed automatically because the shipment is in return, and nothing was changed. For your prioritisation: this is a warranty-repaired spindle drive the workshop has been without for five weeks, nobody contacted the business before the return was triggered, and the repairer says a return would need a fresh export declaration and about three more weeks. I have not told the consignee the return is stopped. Please confirm either way before the trunk departs.
